output.brief: What is going on: the VA-220 failures are mainly caused by defective 2026-built Pellacott valves, not by the new installers or firmware 4.2. Installer and firmware groups fail at the same rate (about 41 vs 42 and 40 vs 42 per 1,000), and Durrant-Hale valves are clean. The defect is a leaking slide seat in Pellacott's 2026 valves. Pellacott's certificates do not reflect real testing. Its leak rig LT-04 has been out of service since 9 January 2026, the 2026 certificates repeat a few identical value sequences, and the "backup rig" was never shown. That is why its score rose. How sure: fairly sure about the installer, firmware and certificate findings. Less sure whether the Corlin seal change is the cause, since it is confounded with the move to Line 3, and I did not check other suppliers. What to do now: quarantine all 2026 Pellacott VA-220 stock, including the six held lots. Suspend its dock-to-stock status. Test valves with Brenmoor's own helium leak test. Do not release the held lots on Pellacott's certificates. Do not charge back installers. Examine the other suppliers' test records before relying on them. Then test the seal material.
